doc.title: Arara · Barra Grande and Machadinho seen by NISAR
hero.kicker: Barra Grande and Machadinho · Pelotas and Uruguay rivers, RS/SC · June to October 2026
hero.title: In {days} days of winter rain, two low reservoirs ({bg_vol0}% and {ma_vol0}%) filled up. The radar measures day or night, regardless of clouds.
hero.dek: Between {r0} and {r1} 2026, Barra Grande rose {bg_rise_m} m (from {bg_vol0}% to {bg_vol1}% of its live storage) and Machadinho rose {ma_rise_m} m (from {ma_vol0}% to {ma_vol1}%). NASA–ISRO's NISAR passed over both reservoirs {n} times from {d0} to {d1}. We measured the water area on each pass with the method validated at Furnas and checked every number against the official ANA water level.
badge.reason: NISAR sees the refill but measures less area than ANA on every date: mean absolute error {bg_mae}% (Barra Grande) and {ma_mae}% (Machadinho), above the {erro_max}% bar.
stat.bg.p: new water seen by NISAR. ANA's level–area curve expects +{bg_cav} km².
stat.ma.p: new water seen by NISAR. ANA's curve expects +{ma_cav} km².
stat.err.p: The timing is right, but NISAR captures only about {bg_ratio}% and {ma_ratio}% of the change in area.
time.title: Watch the water climb into the canyons
time.p1: Each frame is one NISAR pass: HH backscatter in grey (dark = calm water), the water counted by Arara in blue, and the official ANA reservoir outline in yellow. Press play or drag the slider. The jump happens between {r0} and {r1}.
time.flag.rise: Light blue: water on {r1} that was not water on {r0}.
time.flag.wind: Water brighter than usual: possible wind.
time.legend: Light blue in the “new water” view = pixels that became water between {r0} and {r1}; dark blue = water on both dates.
chart.title: Right direction, about half the size
chart.p1: The solid line is the area NISAR measured. The dashed line is the area ANA's level–area curve expects for the official water level on the same day. The shaded band marks the {r0}–{r1} refill. Click a point to move the map to that date.
chart.unit: water area, km² (same scale in both panels)
table.title: Date by date
table.p1: Level and storage come from ANA SAR. The expected area is the ANA curve at that level, applied to the part of the outline the radar measures. No date met the pre-set wind criterion (wind dates: {wind}).
lim.title: Why this study is labelled experimental
lim.p1: The NISAR products (collection NISAR_L2_GCOV_PROVISIONAL_V1, CRID {crid}) are provisional, and calibration may still change. The ANA levels are the operational daily series.
lim.p2: Both reservoirs are canyons a few hundred metres wide. With {px} m pixels and a 5×5 filter, shorelines and narrow arms get lost: NISAR stays below ANA on every date, and the gap grows as the lake fills. At 20 m (sensitivity only, not the result), the error drops to {s_bg_5}% and {s_ma_5}% with the 5×5 filter and {s_bg_3}% and {s_ma_3}% with 3×3, still above 5%, and NISAR stays below ANA when the lakes are full. Newly flooded vegetation, which looks bright to the radar, is a probable but unverified second cause.
lim.p3: The product came without a shadow mask. Slopes facing away from the radar or toward it were estimated from the terrain-correction factor and masked: Barra Grande loses {bg_shadow}% (shadow) + {bg_layover}% (layover) of its outline, plus {bg_out}% outside the swath; Machadinho loses {ma_shadow}% + {ma_layover}%. Valid coverage on every date: {bg_valid}% and {ma_valid}%.
lim.p4: Wind roughens water and makes it brighter, so it can hide from the radar. No date passed the pre-set criterion (water ≥ 1.5 dB brighter than the series median). The brightest date, {bright_date}, reached {bg_bright} dB in Barra Grande and {ma_bright} dB in Machadinho, and is flagged in the notes but kept in the numbers.
src.method: Method: Arara {algo}, the method validated at Furnas (the flood monitor uses version 0.3.0): HH linear power → dB once → 5×5 mean in dB → one threshold for the whole series ({limiar} dB, valley between water and land) → water counted only inside the official outline, no buffer → patches < 0.1 km² removed. GCOV mask values 0 and 255 treated as invalid. Code: pipeline/scripts/estudo_uruguai.py.
